Check a stored dataset

Source: R/check.R
store_check.Rd

Two checks, chosen by x:

Usage

store_check(
  st,
  dataset,
  x = NULL,
  n = 20,
  columns = NULL,
  locations = "all",
  error = TRUE
)

Arguments

st

A store connection made by store_connect().

dataset

The dataset's full name, or its last part when that is unique.

x

NULL for the integrity check, or the data the dataset was written from (data frame, sf object or SpatRaster) for the serialization check.

n

Rows (or raster cells) compared per file.

columns

NULL for all columns that x and the files share, or the names of the columns to compare.

locations

"all" for every available location, or addresses of locations of the connection.

error

TRUE aborts when a check fails; FALSE only reports.

Value

A tibble, invisibly, with one row per location and file: location, dataset, path, status ("ok", "failed", or "missing" when the location does not hold the dataset) and problem (a description, NA when ok).

Details

  • With x, a serialization check: for each file of the dataset, n rows of one random row group are read and compared, column by column, with the matching rows of x: matched by the key, else by .rcs_id, else (tables without key) by row order. Values are compared exactly, after normalisation (a tibble and a data frame are alike, geometries are compared as WKB, times as instants). Geospatial data without key and without a column .rcs_id are geocoded again to find the row identifiers, which matches only a dataset written in one call (not after an update). For a raster, see "Rasters". store_write() runs this check on the staged files before it uploads them.

  • Without x, an integrity check of each location: every file of the current version exists with the MD5 its catalog records (read from the backend's metadata, so no data file is downloaded where the backend reports MD5), its Parquet footer has the recorded rows and the columns of the entry, the version is the hash of the file rows, the totals match, and the manifest agrees with the catalog. The dataset's index table is checked with it.

The catalogs of the checked locations are read again first, and the connection is updated with them.

Rasters

  • With x, a terra::SpatRaster: the stored file must have the layer names and the number of cells of x, and n random cells are compared, layer by layer, as a read returns them. A categorical layer is compared by its codes, not its labels. Cells of x that hold the dataset's NoData value count as missing, as they are in the file (after store_write(nodata = 0), a 0 in x equals a missing cell of the file). A layer stored in single precision (FLT4S) may differ from x by a relative 1e-6; every other type must be equal. The legend and the colours are not compared: they are in the catalog, not in the file. The file is opened through GDAL and only the sampled cells are read.

  • Without x: the file exists with the MD5 its catalog records, the version and the totals match, and the manifest agrees with the catalog. The checks of Parquet footers do not apply to a raster.

See also

store_write().

Examples

root <- file.path(tempdir(), "rcs-example-check")
st <- store_connect(file.path(root, "primary"), create = TRUE)
sales <- rcs_sim_table(100, seed = 1)
store_write(st, sales, "sales/daily",
  title = "Daily sales", description = "Simulated daily sales.",
  key = c("shop_id", "date", "product"), partition = "year"
)
#> ℹ Writing "sales/daily": 100 rows in 2 files (partition year).
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-check/primary  2/2
#>   files sent  23.8 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 2 files in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
store_check(st, "sales/daily")
#> ✔ 2 files checked in 1 location: no problem found.
store_check(st, "sales/daily", x = sales)
#> ✔ 2 files checked in 1 location: no problem found.

# A class map written with `nodata = 0`: the cells of `x` that hold 0
# equal the missing cells of the file, and codes are compared with codes
if (requireNamespace("terra", quietly = TRUE)) {
  cover <- terra::as.int(rcs_sim_raster(nrow = 60, ncol = 80)[["cover"]])
  cover[1:2, ] <- 0L
  levels(cover) <- data.frame(
    value = 1:5,
    label = c("water", "forest", "crop", "grass", "bare")
  )
  names(cover) <- "cover"
  store_write(st, cover, "grids/cover",
    title = "Land cover", description = "A simulated class map.",
    nodata = 0
  )
  store_check(st, "grids/cover")
  store_check(st, "grids/cover", x = cover, n = 500)
}
#> ℹ Writing "grids/cover": 4,800 cells in 1 file.
#> ✔ primary  /tmp/Rtmp/rcs-example-check/primary  1/1
#>   files sent  1.9 kB  0.2s
#> ✔ MD5 identical for 1 file in 1 location. Catalogs updated.
#> ✔ 1 file checked in 1 location: no problem found.
#> ✔ 1 file checked in 1 location: no problem found.
unlink(root, recursive = TRUE)
